An analyst asked this question about an old company annual report (year ended 30 September 1977):

QUESTION: Analyze fixed assets

The report has standalone accounts only. Its primary statements (Profit and Loss Account, Balance Sheet) are always provided with the answer, so don't choose them. Choose from these other parts:
- SCH-x: schedules forming part of the Balance Sheet or the Profit and Loss Account
- Nn: numbered notes to the accounts. Many have no title; the text after the dash is their first words.
- DIR / AUD / SUM / CHR: the Directors' Report, Auditors' Report, Financial Summary and Chairman's Statement

SCHEDULES:
SCH-A: Share Capital (part of the Balance Sheet)  [sub-headings: Authorised; Issued & Subscribed]
SCH-B: Reserves & Surplus (part of the Balance Sheet)
SCH-C: Secured Loans (part of the Balance Sheet)  [sub-headings: From Banks; From Others]
SCH-D: Unsecured Loans (part of the Balance Sheet)
SCH-E: Fixed Assets (part of the Balance Sheet)  [sub-headings: Notes: 1. The figure of Additions to Plant & Machinery includes Rs. 4,57,359/- being machinery-await]

SCH-G: Current Assets (part of the Balance Sheet)
SCH-H: Loans & Advances (part of the Balance Sheet)
SCH-I: Current Liabilities & Provisions (part of the Balance Sheet)

SUGGESTED BY THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS - the statement lines your question is about are linked to these notes (a hint only; choose on the notes' content):
- SCH-E: 6. FIXED ASSETS (Balance Sheet)

Choose the parts whose content is needed to answer the question thoroughly.
- Choose the primary schedule(s) and note(s) first.
- Add the Directors' Report or the Auditors' Report when they are likely to discuss the matter (for example tax disputes, expansion plans, borrowings, audit qualifications), and the Financial Summary for multi-year trends.
- Choose a whole notes schedule only when the question needs most of its notes; otherwise choose individual notes.
- Choose at most 6 items, and prefer fewer.
